messages.content:
The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Looking at this problem, I need to understand what invariant structure is preserved and what the final configuration looks like.

## Key Invariant: Prime Exponent Multisets

When replacing $(a, b)$ with $(\gcd(a,b), \operatorname{lcm}(a,b))$, for each prime $p$:
- If $a$ has $p$-exponent $\alpha$ and $b$ has $p$-exponent $\beta$, the new exponents are $\min(\alpha,\beta)$ and $\max(\alpha,\beta)$

So **for each prime $p$, the multiset of exponents across all 2100 numbers is invariant.**

## Final State Characterization

The process stops when no move changes the board, which means every pair $(a,b)$ satisfies $a \mid b$ or $b \mid a$. Since there are 2100 numbers, the final state is a chain:
$$n_1 \mid n_2 \mid \cdots \mid n_{2100}$$

For each prime $p$, the exponents must be non-decreasing: $e_1(p) \leq e_2(p) \leq \cdots \leq e_{2100}(p)$. Since the multiset is invariant, $e_k(p)$ is the **$k$-th smallest** value in $\{v_p(1), v_p(2), \ldots, v_p(2100)\}$.

## Computing the 2026th Smallest Number

Since $n_1 \mid n_2 \mid \cdots \mid n_{2100}$, we have $n_1 \leq n_2 \leq \cdots \leq n_{2100}$, so the 2026th smallest number is $n_{2026}$.

For each prime $p$, I need the 2026th smallest $p$-exponent. The number of $k \in \{1,\ldots,2100\}$ with $v_p(k) \geq j$ is $\lfloor 2100/p^j \rfloor$.

The 2026th value equals $j$ when:
- $\lfloor 2100/p^j \rfloor > 74$ (at least 75 elements have exponent $\geq j$)
- $\lfloor 2100/p^{j+1} \rfloor \leq 74$ (at most 74 elements have exponent $\geq j+1$)

This gives: $p^j \leq 28 < p^{j+1}$, so $e_{2026}(p) = \max\{j : p^j \leq 28\}$.

## Computing Each Exponent

| Prime $p$ | $p^j \leq 28$ | $e_{2026}(p)$ |
|-----------|---------------|---------------|
| 2 | $2^4 = 16 \leq 28$, $2^5 = 32 > 28$ | 4 |
| 3 | $3^3 = 27 \leq 28$, $3^4 = 81 > 28$ | 3 |
| 5 | $5^2 = 25 \leq 28$, $5^3 = 125 > 28$ | 2 |
| 7 | $7^1 = 7 \leq 28$, $7^2 = 49 > 28$ | 1 |
| 11 | $11^1 = 11 \leq 28$, $11^2 > 28$ | 1 |
| 13 | $13^1 = 13 \leq 28$, $13^2 > 28$ | 1 |
| 17 | $17^1 = 17 \leq 28$, $17^2 > 28$ | 1 |
| 19 | $19^1 = 19 \leq 28$, $19^2 > 28$ | 1 |
| 23 | $23^1 = 23 \leq 28$, $23^2 > 28$ | 1 |
| $p \geq 29$ | $p > 28$ | 0 |

## Result

$$n_{2026} = 2^4 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 7^1 \cdot 11^1 \cdot 13^1 \cdot 17^1 \cdot 19^1 \cdot 23^1$$

The number of divisors is:
$$(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6 = 5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2^6 = 60 \times 64 = 3840$$

$$\boxed{3840}$$
